purpose: Answer brianosaurus's scoping question on vllm-project/vllm#52530 (pullrequestreview-4946863171): does the decode case -- prompt + max_tokens crossing max_servable_num_tokens after admission -- livelock like #52520, or is it bounded? Measure on unmodified upstream main, then make the PR's scope match the measurement.

reviewer_question.substance: _is_unservable bounds on request.num_tokens + 1, but a generate request grows to prompt + max_tokens. With max_model_len=8192 and max_servable_num_tokens=8000, prompt=7000/max_tokens=1000 clears the frontend and clears _is_unservable, then needs a block the pool does not have at token 8000. Deliberately out of scope? If the gap can be wide, bound on num_tokens + max_tokens for generate requests.

measurement.verdict: (a) LIVELOCK -- reproduced on unmodified upstream main. The decode case is the same defect, not a deliberate exclusion.
measurement.hardware: CPU only, no GPU, no model weights (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""); scheduler driven directly through schedule()/update_from_output()
measurement.how_main_was_restored: git checkout 4d2a68d64d9e05921ed5c4099146e768a92d71d5 -- vllm/ in /var/tmp/vllm-52520 (branch tests kept, no vllm/ source from the branch present); verified 0 occurrences of max_servable_num_tokens in vllm/ before each stock run
measurement.argv: EXTRA_PYTHONPATH=/var/tmp/vllm-52520 /var/tmp/rootfs-shim/py3 /home/mbelleau/research/upstream/repro-52520-decode-stock-main.py  (cwd /var/tmp/vllm-52520; HF_HOME=/var/tmp/hf-home-3 on the reruns, to stop the 429 that the sweep's ModelConfig constructions trigger)

configuration.note: the gate-zero config from upstream/repro-52520-stock-main.py, scaled only by splitting the sequence across the prefill/decode boundary
configuration.kv_cache_groups: KVCacheGroupSpec(['fa'], FullAttentionSpec(block_size=16, num_kv_heads=1, head_size=1, float32)) + KVCacheGroupSpec(['mamba'], MambaSpec(block_size=16, shapes=((1,1),), float32, mamba_cache_mode='align', num_speculative_blocks=3, page_size_padded=fa.page_size_bytes))
configuration.pool_blocks_rationale: cdiv(1024,16)=64 attention + (2+3)=5 mamba = 69; get_kv_cache_configs accepts exactly 69
configuration.why_that_request: frontend 1000+24=1024 <= max_model_len 1024 -> accepted; _is_unservable 1000+1=1001 <= 1008 -> admitted; sequence reaches 1024 > 1008 during decode. brianosaurus's 7000/1000/8000/8192 example, one order of magnitude down.

measurement.observation_window: 4000 scheduler steps for every run; each run stops early only when the request finishes. Steps 13..3999 (3987 steps) of the failing run scheduled zero tokens, produced zero output tokens and freed nothing.
trace_at_the_wall_stock_main: step 11 sched=1 computed=1007 seq_len=1008 out=8 free=1  RUNNING   preempt=0 ev=0
step 12 sched=1 computed=1008 seq_len=1009 out=9 free=1  RUNNING   preempt=0 ev=0
step 13 sched=0 computed=0    seq_len=1009 out=9 free=68 PREEMPTED preempt=1 ev=1
measurement.preemption_counter_note: vllm:num_preemptions_total increments exactly ONCE and then stops -- it does not climb. metrics/stats.py:449 counts EngineCoreEventType.PREEMPTED events; the request records one at scheduler.py:1404 and is then 1009 tokens long, which is past the 1008 the pool can re-prefill, so it is never scheduled again. The decode case collapses into the prefill case of #52520 rather than having a distinct signature. This corrects the 'num_preemptions_total climbing' shape assumed in the acknowledgement comment.
measurement.controls: control-pool+1 (70 blocks, same request) finishes 24/24 in 28 steps with 0 preemptions; control-under-ceiling (69 blocks, max_tokens=8) finishes 8/8 in 12 steps with 0 preemptions. So neither the harness nor the 69-block pool is what fails -- only crossing the ceiling.
measurement.spec_lookahead_probe: With drafts injected (request.spec_token_ids = [7,7,7] each step, which the scheduler reads at sched/scheduler.py:737 and turns into 1+len slots), the running path CAN reach past the ceiling before the length cap fires. Measured on stock main: 2 preemptions, then FINISHED_LENGTH_CAPPED 8/8 at step 13. Bounded and self-correcting, because preemption clears spec_token_ids (sched/scheduler.py:1389) and the retry decodes one token at a time. Identical on the branch. Therefore scheduler.py:605 was NOT changed.

gap_width.question: how wide can max_model_len - max_servable_num_tokens get, as a function of configuration
gap_width.answer: Exactly one block, never more, and only when the pool is at the startup minimum. gap = ((max_model_len - 1) mod block_size) + 1 tokens, i.e. whatever max_model_len occupies in its last block; 0 as soon as the pool has one block more. Measured across 14 configurations on unmodified main; the largest gap observed was 256 tokens at block_size=256, and every gap was exactly 1.00 blocks or 0.

contributors.worth: the entire gap: one block, always
file_line: vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:2193 (_check_enough_kv_cache_memory is handed the byte count for ALL blocks)
contributors.evidence: the same check also refuses any pool below the minimum, so the shortfall is one block or nothing

contributors.worth: decides how many of that block's tokens are lost: block_size when max_model_len divides evenly, ((max_model_len-1) mod block_size)+1 otherwise
contributors.evidence: sweep rows max_model_len 1000 -> gap 8 and 1009 -> gap 1 at block_size 16

file_line: vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py:694 (MambaSpec.max_memory_usage_bytes = page_size * (2 + num_speculative_blocks) in align mode)
contributors.evidence: priced identically on both sides of the comparison, so it moves the requirement and the ceiling together; sweep rows block_size 16 / max_model_len 1024 with num_speculative_blocks 3 and 0 both give gap 16. This corrects the claim in issuecomment-5308876923 that the speculative reserve widens the gap.

contributors.contributor: one spare block closes it entirely

gap_width.verdict_on_reviewer_framing: The reviewer's magnitude was right and his mechanism was not: 8064 vs 8192 at block_size=128 is within touching distance of the 8000/8192 he wrote by hand, but it comes from one block, not from an accumulation of null block + speculative reserve + rounding.

decision.chosen: Apply the pool's ceiling as a LENGTH CAP at the point of exhaustion: check_stop(request, self.max_servable_num_tokens) instead of check_stop(request, self.max_model_len).
decision.rejected_option_a: Bound admission on num_tokens + max_tokens for generate requests (the reviewer's suggestion). Rejected because it refuses requests that would stop long before the wall: control-under-ceiling above is exactly that request (prompt=1000, max_tokens=8) and it runs to completion on the same pool. Callers routinely set max_tokens an order of magnitude above what the model emits, so this is a behaviour change on a common path, not a bug fix.
decision.rejected_option_b: Fail the request with an error at the point of exhaustion. Rejected because by then the client has already been streamed 8 tokens; finish_reason 'length' is the truthful reason (the sequence hit a context limit, just a lower one than advertised), and the actionable operator-facing form already exists once, at startup, in the logger.error that names the ceiling.
decision.why_it_is_safe: max_servable_num_tokens <= max_model_len by construction (_estimate_max_model_len_from_groups searches with right = original_max, kv_cache_utils.py:1960) and the scheduler falls back to max_model_len when there is no per-block bound to price, so on every pool that covers its window this is the same call it was.
decision.shape: one bound, three call sites: startup sizing, admission, length cap
